incident-bot: ALERT detected: unusual spike in kv-cache memory + increased tail latency on serving nodes in us-west-2. Error pattern looks like cache reuse with stale seq offsets. Alert rule: kv_cache.reuse.err_rate > 0.5% for 5m.

Morgan (oncall): I see the alert, pulling traces now. Which customers hit it?

Eva (support): Support reports 2 customers on Dedicated saw requests timing out ~30s and 504s. Tickets created — customer A and customer B.

Jia (eng-runtime): logs show a repeat of the old reuse pattern: keys from previous requests being returned for different session ids. Suspect paging + continuous batching interaction. Sample log:```[2026-03-14T21:12:03Z] req=0x7f3 kv_lookup key=ctx_123 seq=42 -> value seq=36 (mismatch)```

Samir (eng-sre): If seq offsets are wrong, KV cache index could be reusing slots without invalidation. Quick mitigation: disable kv reuse at runtime or fall back to per-request cache.

Morgan (oncall): Can we flip a flag? What's the safest hotfix?

Jia (eng-runtime): Two levers: 1) disable `kv_reuse_enabled` (fast), 2) throttle continuous batching (`continuous_batching.max_batch_size = 1`) (heavier perf impact). I recommend flipping the kv reuse flag first.

Morgan (oncall): Do it. Javier (ops) — please coordinate with deploy bot.

Samir (eng-sre): I'm creating a page to change the runtime flag via the config API. Patch request:```PATCH /admin/runtime-flags
{ "kv_reuse_enabled": false }```

Diego (oncall): I'll take the patch and run in canary (2 nodes) then promote. Starting canary now.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for runtime-flags v2026.3.14-rc1 to cluster us-west-2-canary.

Jia (eng-runtime): Watch for latency regressions on p95. If we see severe perf cliff, we fall back to throttling batching instead.

(10m later)

Diego (oncall): Canary looks good — memory growth stopped, error rate dropped to baseline. Promoting to prod.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: rollout 50% -> 100% over 12m.

Eva (support): Customers A and B confirm service is returning to normal. Liza (cs) pinged both.

Morgan (oncall): Observed spike in CPU while flag was off (expected). p95 latency rose ~10-15% for small requests, overall error rate back to normal.

Jia (eng-runtime): Root cause theory: paging introduced a path that reused KV slab indices without resetting seq offsets when pages were evicted and reallocated. Under continuous batching the timing window allowed cross-request reuse. We'll need a proper fix: ensure seq increment semantics are stored alongside slot, and verify eviction logic zeroes seq metadata.

Samir (eng-sre): Short postmortem action items: 1) add invariant check in runtime: assert(slot.seq == request.seq) 2) add e2e test covering paging + continuous batching 3) add metric `kv_slot_seq_mismatch` alert.

Diego (oncall): Handoff to Morgan -> Diego taking oncall next 2 hours to monitor rollback effects and customer followups. Morgan handing over.

Morgan (oncall): Handoff acknowledged. Key notes: flag turned off at 2123456860, rollout completed by 2123457000. Customers notified. Monitor p99 and kv_slot_seq_mismatch.

Liza (cs): I'll keep CS loop open, prepping customer post-incident summary and ETA for permanent fix.

Jia (eng-runtime): Plan for permanent patch: change slot metadata layout and add atomic seq compare/replace on cache reuse. ETA: 3 working days + canary. Will open PR and link to this thread.

Samir (eng-sre): For next 24h monitoring: enable verbose kv-slot logs at 1% sampling. Command:```kubectl exec -c runtime svc/serve -- /bin/sh -c \"echo 'kv_slot_log_sample=0.01' > /proc/runtime/flags\"```

incident-bot: Annotated incident: INC-2026-0314-KV-REUSE created, severity: high -> mitigated.

Diego (oncall): I'll run a synthetic workload exercise after handoff to verify no regression under batching. Morgan, tagging you on the follow-up postmortem once PR lands.

Morgan (oncall): Thanks everyone. We'll update the incident timeline and add the customer impact table. Closing active mitigation — monitoring until 2123460389.
